newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Guinea-Bissau cholera death toll rises to 383.
newsitem.headline: Guinea-Bissau cholera death toll rises to 383.

text.p: A cholera outbreak in the West African state of Guinea-Bissau has killed 383 people and 16,868 cases have been reported since authorities declared an epidemic last October, the Portuguese news agency reported on Wednesday.
Most of the cases registered so far were in and near Bissau, capital of the former Portuguese colony, Lusa said in a report from Bissau, quoting health ministry officials.
The previous cholera epidemic in Guinea-Bissau, which lasted from October 1994 to March 1995, killed 290 people.

Cholera, spread by poor hygiene or the contamination of drinking water by sewage, brings on severe diarrhoea and dehydration and kills if not treated quickly. Outbreaks often coincide with the rainy season in West Africa.
The disease is relatively easy to treat but health workers say rehydration fluids and medicines are in short supply.
